text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bodies litter the streets in southwest Nigerian city of Ife after community clashes.
- The fuel supply to the administrative capital Abuja has improved after weeks of shortages.
- The Department of Petroleum Resources has promoted 250 workers in a bid to quell rising tension in the oil industry's supervisory body.
- Members of traditional courts in southeastern Abia state have been banned from drinking beer and palm wine in local bars to preserve local respect for the judiciary.

- International inspection agencies Cotecna and SGS, appointed by Nigeria's government last year, have embarked on plans to ensure their survival since the ending of their contracts. Measures include cutting back staff and stoppage of allowances.
- Central bank says that from now on only bank transactions in bankers' acceptances and commercial papers will be treated as on-balance-sheet items and counted as part of a bank's credit portfolio.
- Head of State General Sani Abacha meets Ivory Coast President Henri Konan Bedie over crisis in Sierra Leone.

- Plans have been concluded by Nigeria Television and Telecom International, in conjuction with British Telecom to build, operate and manage a new telecommunications network in Nigeria which will provide 100,000 new lines within a year in the Lagos business districts of Ikeja and Apapa.
- Nigeria Airways is likely to ground pilots who also have a role in management.

- Nigeria's biggest banks, Union Bank, UBA, Afribank and First Bank are to meet next week to discuss ways of getting around a central bank threat to penalise banks which do not sort their currency into usable and unusable notes.
- Accounts of some ministries and parastatals are yet to be credited with this year's capital expenditure, two weeks after the order was given for the release of the money by the finance ministry.
